title: Library assembly: 3 part lists into DMX-demo
summary: Join 72 synthesised parts into 13824 distinct constructs in 3 rounds. Each round opens the library with BbsI, releases one part list with BsaI, ligates the two, and transforms, grows and preps the result for the round after it.
highlights: One round appends one part list to every member of the library at once, so 3 rounds make 13824 constructs out of 72 synthesised parts.
The product keeps BbsI's sites, which is what lets the next round open it, and loses BsaI's with the external stuffers.
Your vector already carried an internal stuffer, so every part enters position N on AGGA, which is the overhang that stuffer spells: DNA that exists cannot be re-chosen.
The overhang standard changes 27 amino acid(s) across 26 part end(s); changes.tsv has wild type beside synthesised, and that is what you are about to pay for.
The last round needs 4,147,200 colonies for 300x coverage of its 13,824 products. A round short of that loses members no later round can put back.
The finished barcode block is 41 bp and reads in the reverse of the order the rounds ran; barcodes.tsv says which barcode names which part.

rules.subject: PEG
rules.detail: Never add PEG to a T7 ligase reaction. Blunt-end ligation is forced above 20% (w/v) PEG 6000, and StickTogether buffer already carries 7.5%; the refusal that removes escapees holds only while nothing adds more.

rules.subject: heat inactivation
rules.detail: Do not heat-inactivate T7 DNA ligase in PEG: transformation will be inhibited. Go from the ligation straight to the clean-up.

steps.title: Order the oligo pool and the primers that amplify it
instructions: Order every row of pool.tsv as one synthesised oligo pool, 153 members at 350 nt.
Order every row of pool-primers.tsv as an ordinary oligo: 1 P1 batch forward, 72 P2 gene reverse, 1 P3 batch outer.
notes: pool.tsv names each oligo's block, which piece of it that is, and the primers that pull it out, so an oligo is traceable to its protein.
152 oligos is what the length budget allows for; this design spends 153, one more on N_ATF7, whose forced cuts spell no legal overhang.
expected: One pool, 153 oligos, every one 350 nt and no length spread, which is what the padding is for.
74 primers, each 20 nt.

troubleshooting.problem: The vendor bins the pool by length
troubleshooting.solution: Every oligo is padded to one length, so the spread is zero. A vendor asking for a different length wants the project's oligo length changed and the design run again.

steps.title: PCR1: pull 1 batch out of the pool
instructions: Set up 1 reaction, one a batch, with the pool as template.
Give each its own pair: batch 1: OP107 with OP146.
Run the program below. On a real-time instrument, add an intercalating dye and stop before the curve plateaus; the printed count is what to run without one.
notes: Every pair anneals at 65.1 °C, so one block of tubes takes them all.

Twist's band for a 350 nt pool is 12 to 14 cycles; Twist Oligo Pools Amplification Protocol DOC-4060 REV 1.0 gives the same three bands. Its FAQ answers that more cycles give worse uniformity, so 12 is what prints.
The outer primer is what makes a batch a batch: it is dropped at PCR2, so a block cannot be pulled out of a batch it does not sit in.
expected: One band at 350 bp in every batch, which is the whole oligo.
Batch sizes: 1 holds 72.

troubleshooting.solution: Drop the annealing temperature by 3 °C and check the pool went in.

troubleshooting.problem: A hump after the peak on a Bioanalyzer or TapeStation trace
troubleshooting.solution: Heteroduplexes, which is what over-amplification leaves. Run it again with fewer cycles. What too many cycles cost is dropout, chimeras and polymerase error; pooling the blocks equimolar later restores the evenness but none of those.

holes.missing: no cycle count published for Q5 on a Twist oligo pool
holes.where: PCR1, the polymerase the cycle count is stated against
holes.filled_by: a count Twist states against Q5, or a pilot on this pool

steps.title: PCR2: pull each of the 72 blocks out of its batch
instructions: Set up one reaction a block, 72 in all, in PCR2 plate.
Give each its batch's PCR1 product as template, that batch's forward primer, and the block's own inner primer.
Run the program below. Nobody published a cycle count for this reaction, so run it on a real-time instrument with an intercalating dye and stop before the curve plateaus.
notes: The pairs anneal between 64.3 and 65.1 °C. The program runs at 64.3, the lowest of them, so one block of tubes takes them all.
A block is named by its well from here on, not by anything in the tube.
expected: One band at 330 bp in every well, the outer primer's 20 nt shorter than PCR1's.
72 wells filled across 1 plate.

troubleshooting.solution: The outer primer region was not dropped. Check the inner primer went in, and that the template is PCR1's product and not the pool.

troubleshooting.problem: A hump after the peak on a Bioanalyzer or TapeStation trace
troubleshooting.solution: Heteroduplexes, which is what over-amplification leaves. Run it again with fewer cycles; the forward primer is the whole batch's, so over-cycling here also pulls a neighbour's product into the well.

holes.missing: no cycle count for PCR2, which pulls one block out of an already-amplified batch
holes.filled_by: a pilot titrated against the heteroduplex hump on capillary electrophoresis, or a real-time run stopped before the curve plateaus

steps.title: Assemble each block from its 1 to 5 pieces
instructions: Set up one BsmBI assembly a well, holding that block's own PCR2 pieces and nothing from another well.
notes: BsmBI cuts each oligo back to its fragment, so the primer sites, the recognition sites and the padding all stay outside the block.
expected: 72 blocks, 133 to 1149 bp, as parts.tsv spells them.
Each block reads: 5' external stuffer, coding bases, internal stuffer, barcode, 3' external stuffer.

troubleshooting.solution: A piece was missing from the well. Check that well's PCR2 lane before assembling it again; the pieces of one block are not interchangeable.

holes.missing: nothing names what the assembled pieces close into, or what selects the closure
holes.filled_by: a destination the pieces assemble into, as the method's DMX vector is for cargo carrying no flanks of its own

holes.missing: no source sets the DNA in, the enzyme, the ligase or the cycling for a block assembly
holes.where: block assembly, the reaction and its program
holes.filled_by: NEB's own Golden Gate table, once the assembly has a destination to be sized against

steps.title: Array 72 design(s) and grow
instructions: Spot each design from its archive plate as its own spot on a 25 cm BioAssay plate.
Grow overnight at 37 °C on 100 µg/mL carbenicillin.
notes: This project reads back every design, which a floor of zero does: 72 design(s). The rest stay polyclonal and are never read one design at a time.
The archive is untouched: this reads a copy of it.
expected: One spot a design, at about 2,500 colonies a plate, which is the density picking wants.

troubleshooting.solution: That design has no clone to read. Re-transform it from the archive before anyone re-synthesises it.

steps.title: Pick 4 colonies of each design
instructions: Pick 4 colonies a design into 60 µL low-salt LB with carbenicillin, with the QPix XE Microbial Colony Picker.
Fill one quarter of each 384-well plate before starting the next.
Grow overnight at 37 °C.
notes: 4 colonies a design is Lund's anchor and the only measured one; four gave a clean copy of 343 of 458 genes.
1 fragment(s): 21 design(s), 100.0% of picks clean
2 fragment(s): 34 design(s), 100.0% of picks clean
3 fragment(s): 6 design(s), 93.8% of picks clean
4 fragment(s): 9 design(s), 89.2% of picks clean
5 fragment(s): 2 design(s), 84.6% of picks clean
A quarter at a time is what makes a part-filled plate give full plates downstream, and what keeps a mark off a plate that is mostly empty.
expected: 288 wells over 1 plate(s): 288 picked.
Every colony of one design sits on one plate.

troubleshooting.problem: A design in many fragments gives no clean colony
troubleshooting.solution: The chances above say which designs that is likeliest for. Pick more colonies of those designs before the plates are poured, not after.

steps.title: Sample the picked plates into index plates
instructions: Move 1 µL of each well into its 96-well plate, one quarter of the picked plate a pass.
notes: One well in four lines up under a head built for the smaller format, so a quarter moves in one pass.

transfers.title: Sample a quarter of picked 1 into index 1
transfers.note: one well in four, which is the spacing a head built for the index format reads

transfers.title: Sample a quarter of picked 1 into index 2
transfers.note: one well in four, which is the spacing a head built for the index format reads

transfers.title: Sample a quarter of picked 1 into index 3
transfers.note: one well in four, which is the spacing a head built for the index format reads

expected: 3 index plate(s), 288 reactions in all.

steps.title: Amplify each well with its own pair
instructions: Add 7 µL of the master mix below to each well, which already holds its 1 µL of culture.
Add 2 µL of the pair its address names from the prepared primer plate, for 10 µL a well.
Seal the plate, spin it down, and run the program below.
notes: 96 forward marks and 96 reverse reach 9,216 wells, so the pairs already held cover far more than this run needs.
The primer plate is built once as lab stock and a run calls for it; this protocol does not build one.
The first 10 cycles touch down from 68 to 63.5 °C, 0.5 °C a cycle, and 25 more run at 68 °C.
Extension is 2 minutes, what the authors ran for a gene below 1 kb. The published rule is at least one minute a kilobase, so a longer design wants it raised.
The mix is made 1.5 times what the wells take, which is what LevSeq's own per-plate table spells out. Nothing says what the surplus is for.

tables.title: Index PCR, one well a sample

expected: One barcoded amplicon a well. Well *n* of a plate takes forward mark *n*, and every well of one plate takes that plate's own reverse mark.
One band a well, the design plus about 100 bp: the two marks, and the stretch between the primer sites and the reading frame.

troubleshooting.problem: A plate reads back far fewer wells than the others
troubleshooting.solution: LevSeq traces that to the amplification, not the sequencing: on a run of ten plates three returned under 60% of their variants. Check each pool on a gel before the library prep.

holes.missing: no index mark set is named for the barcoded primer pairs
holes.where: route B, the pair marking one well
holes.filled_by: the prepared primer plate the lab holds

holes.missing: the units of Taq one index PCR takes
holes.where: route B, the index PCR's polymerase
holes.filled_by: NEB's own specification for M0267, which gives the stock concentration

steps.title: Pool and sequence
instructions: Pool each index plate on its own and clean the pool up.
Sequence the pool.
notes: Two plates on one flow cell are told apart by construction, because one axis of the address is the plate.
expected: Reads for 288 wells, every well told from the rest by the marks it carries.

steps.title: Call every well
instructions: Demultiplex the reads by address, checking each address rather than trusting a file.
Call a consensus a well, then compare it with that well's design base for base.
Reformat, compacting out the wells that failed.
notes: A well read too thinly carries no verdict and is not a failure, so reformatting does not compact it out.
More than one consensus is mixed, and mixed fails.
A design with no passing well is picked again from the same archive spot before anyone re-synthesises it.
expected: A well read more than 20 times is called; route B tolerates 10 and warns between the two.
A pass matches across the whole designed region: both entry overhangs, the fragment, the stuffer and the barcode.

troubleshooting.problem: A well's call is the right protein and the wrong barcode
troubleshooting.solution: It fails. A barcode that no longer names its member cannot be put right by the linkage read later.

steps.title: Pool each part list
instructions: Resuspend every block and measure each concentration.
Pool the members of each part list in equal molar amounts, one tube per position.
notes: Library coverage is counted on equally represented members, so an uneven pool loses members that no later round can put back.
expected: N: one tube holding 24 member(s).
DBD: one tube holding 24 member(s).
C: one tube holding 24 member(s).

troubleshooting.problem: One member is much more dilute than the rest
troubleshooting.solution: Pool to the lowest member rather than to the mean; a member short here is short in every round after it.

steps.title: Round 1: open DMX-demo with BbsI
instructions: Set the digest below up with BbsI alone, and start the program.
After the first hour add SrfI and run the second.
notes: BbsI is the enzyme the product keeps sites for. That is the design working, not a site left behind.
expected: DMX-demo opens on AGGA and TTCC, leaving 1204 bp of backbone.
The 30 bp internal stuffer comes out, and SrfI cuts it so it cannot go back in.

troubleshooting.solution: The destination was not opened to completion. Run a little of the digest on a gel before ligating the next round.

steps.title: Round 1: release the N part list with BsaI
instructions: Set the digest below up with BsaI alone, and start the program.
After the first hour add PmeI and run the second.
notes: One tube takes the whole part list: every member carries the same stuffers and differs only in its coding bases and its barcode.
The amounts are weighed at the pool's mean block length, 613 bp.
expected: Every member of the N part list is released, about 559 bp, on the same two overhangs the destination now offers.
PmeI cuts the two external stuffers left behind, so neither can ligate back.

troubleshooting.problem: A member is missing from the library later
troubleshooting.solution: Its block was under-represented in the pool, or its own digest was incomplete. Check the pool before repeating the round.

steps.title: Round 1: clean both digests up
instructions: Add 2 volumes of SPRI paramagnetic beads to each digest and elute in water.
Measure both concentrations; the ligation table asks for picomoles, not nanograms.
notes: 2 volumes here and 1 after the ligation. The two ratios differ; they are not one number used twice.
expected: DMX-demo, opened: 0.0269677 pmol is 20 ng at 1204 bp.
N part list, released: 0.0269677 pmol is 9.29 ng at 559 bp.

troubleshooting.solution: Elute in a smaller volume, or scale the ligation up.

steps.title: Round 1: ligate the N part list into the library
instructions: Pipette the two DNAs into the tube first, then the ligase, its buffer and water.
Hold at room temperature for 30 minutes.
notes: Picomoles, not nanograms: the shorter fragment weighs less at the same ratio.
The method names T7 DNA Ligase and StickTogether DNA Ligase Buffer and publishes neither the units nor the volume, so the last line of the table is the supplier's own.

components.name: T7 DNA Ligase in StickTogether DNA Ligase Buffer, and nuclease-free water

expected: Nothing visible. 0.0269677 pmol of the released part list against 0.0269677 pmol of the opened library is the 1:1 molar ratio.

troubleshooting.solution: Check that both digests went to completion; an uncut end cannot ligate.

steps.title: Round 1: clean the ligation up
instructions: Add 1 volume of SPRI paramagnetic beads and elute in water.
Measure the concentration.
notes: One volume here, not the 2 the digests took. Eluting in water rather than a buffer is what keeps the salt out of the cuvette.
expected: Enough for one electroporation: 100 ng is 0.0810933 pmol at 2002 bp.

troubleshooting.solution: Repeat the clean-up; salt carried into the cuvette arcs the pulse.

steps.title: Round 1: electroporate into Endura ElectroCompetent Cells
instructions: Thaw one aliquot of Endura ElectroCompetent Cells on ice, 25 µL a pulse.
Add at most 100 ng of the purified ligation and mix without making bubbles.
Pulse at 1800 V, 600 Ω and 10 µF in a 1 mm cuvette.
cautions: Keep the cells and the cuvette on ice; a warm cuvette arcs.
notes: The method names the instrument and none of the settings, so the program is the cells' own: it is keyed by 60242-2 and changes when the cells do. The materials table says where it was read.
expected: A pulse with no arc, and a time constant of 3.5 to 4.5 ms.

troubleshooting.solution: The DNA carries salt. Clean it up again, elute in water, and use a fresh aliquot of cells.

steps.title: Round 1: recover and grow at 30 °C
instructions: Add recovery medium straight away and shake for the first hour.
Plate a measured dilution of the recovery on selection as round 1 titre, and grow the rest in selective broth.
Plate the no-donor ligation from the same digest as round 1 no-donor control, at the same dilution.
notes: Both steps run at 30 °C and not at 37 °C. That is a library precaution rather than an oversight.
The program carries the shorter outgrowth; 12 to 16 hours is the range the method gives.
300x is the project's own, and follows from the representation the screen downstream asks for. No source sets it, and nothing here defaults it.
The control measures the chain the design rests on — two cuts, a blunt chopper, a ligase that refuses blunt ends and the 2x clean-up — rather than assuming it.
expected: At least 7,200 net colonies, scaled up from the dilution: 24 distinct products this round can make, times the 300x the project asked for, rounded up.
At that count the chance a named product is missing is 8.31e-134.
round 1 no-donor control should be near empty beside it; its colonies come off the count.

troubleshooting.problem: Fewer net colonies than the count above
troubleshooting.solution: The round has lost library members and no later round can put them back. Electroporate more of the ligation, or run the round again.

troubleshooting.problem: The no-donor control is not empty
troubleshooting.solution: The destination was not opened to completion, or the blunt chopper missed. What grows is the round before's library, one position short, and it reaches the linkage read as truncated members.

steps.title: Round 1: prep the library
instructions: Harvest the whole culture rather than a single colony.
Prep the plasmid and measure the concentration.
notes: Harvesting the whole culture is what keeps the library a library; picking colonies here throws away everything not picked.
expected: One pool of plasmid, 2002 bp per molecule. This is the destination round 2 opens.
BbsI still cuts it and BsaI no longer does.

troubleshooting.solution: The culture was grown too briefly, or the antibiotic was wrong for this backbone. Check the vector's own marker.

troubleshooting.solution: The culture was grown too briefly, or the antibiotic was wrong for this backbone. Check the vector's own marker.

steps.title: Round 3: open AP-1 DESynR round 2 with BbsI
instructions: Set the digest below up with BbsI alone, and start the program.
After the first hour add SrfI and run the second.
notes: BbsI is the enzyme the product keeps sites for. That is the design working, not a site left behind.
expected: AP-1 DESynR round 2 opens on GCAT and TTCC, leaving 2179 bp of backbone.
The 30 bp internal stuffer comes out, and SrfI cuts it so it cannot go back in.

troubleshooting.solution: The destination was not opened to completion. Run a little of the digest on a gel before ligating the next round.

steps.title: Round 3: release the C part list with BsaI
instructions: Set the digest below up with BsaI alone, and start the program.
After the first hour add PmeI and run the second.
notes: One tube takes the whole part list: every member carries the same stuffers and differs only in its coding bases and its barcode.
The amounts are weighed at the pool's mean block length, 350 bp.
expected: Every member of the C part list is released, about 296 bp, on the same two overhangs the destination now offers.
PmeI cuts the two external stuffers left behind, so neither can ligate back.

troubleshooting.problem: A member is missing from the library later
troubleshooting.solution: Its block was under-represented in the pool, or its own digest was incomplete. Check the pool before repeating the round.

steps.title: Round 3: clean both digests up
instructions: Add 2 volumes of SPRI paramagnetic beads to each digest and elute in water.
Measure both concentrations; the ligation table asks for picomoles, not nanograms.
notes: 2 volumes here and 1 after the ligation. The two ratios differ; they are not one number used twice.
expected: AP-1 DESynR round 2, opened: 0.0149012 pmol is 20 ng at 2179 bp.
C part list, released: 0.0149012 pmol is 2.72 ng at 296 bp.

troubleshooting.solution: Elute in a smaller volume, or scale the ligation up.

steps.title: Round 3: ligate the C part list into the library
instructions: Pipette the two DNAs into the tube first, then the ligase, its buffer and water.
Hold at room temperature for 30 minutes.
notes: Picomoles, not nanograms: the shorter fragment weighs less at the same ratio.
The method names T7 DNA Ligase and StickTogether DNA Ligase Buffer and publishes neither the units nor the volume, so the last line of the table is the supplier's own.

components.name: T7 DNA Ligase in StickTogether DNA Ligase Buffer, and nuclease-free water

expected: Nothing visible. 0.0149012 pmol of the released part list against 0.0149012 pmol of the opened library is the 1:1 molar ratio.

troubleshooting.solution: Check that both digests went to completion; an uncut end cannot ligate.

steps.title: Round 3: clean the ligation up
instructions: Add 1 volume of SPRI paramagnetic beads and elute in water.
Measure the concentration.
notes: One volume here, not the 2 the digests took. Eluting in water rather than a buffer is what keeps the salt out of the cuvette.
expected: Enough for one electroporation: 100 ng is 0.071331 pmol at 2276 bp.

troubleshooting.solution: Repeat the clean-up; salt carried into the cuvette arcs the pulse.

steps.title: Round 3: electroporate into Endura ElectroCompetent Cells
instructions: Thaw one aliquot of Endura ElectroCompetent Cells on ice, 25 µL a pulse.
Add at most 100 ng of the purified ligation and mix without making bubbles.
Pulse at 1800 V, 600 Ω and 10 µF in a 1 mm cuvette.
cautions: Keep the cells and the cuvette on ice; a warm cuvette arcs.
notes: The method names the instrument and none of the settings, so the program is the cells' own: it is keyed by 60242-2 and changes when the cells do. The materials table says where it was read.
expected: A pulse with no arc, and a time constant of 3.5 to 4.5 ms.

troubleshooting.solution: The DNA carries salt. Clean it up again, elute in water, and use a fresh aliquot of cells.

steps.title: Round 3: recover and grow at 30 °C
instructions: Add recovery medium straight away and shake for the first hour.
Plate a measured dilution of the recovery on selection as round 3 titre, and grow the rest in selective broth.
Plate the no-donor ligation from the same digest as round 3 no-donor control, at the same dilution.
notes: Both steps run at 30 °C and not at 37 °C. That is a library precaution rather than an oversight.
The program carries the shorter outgrowth; 12 to 16 hours is the range the method gives.
300x is the project's own, and follows from the representation the screen downstream asks for. No source sets it, and nothing here defaults it.
The control measures the chain the design rests on — two cuts, a blunt chopper, a ligase that refuses blunt ends and the 2x clean-up — rather than assuming it.
expected: At least 4,147,200 net colonies, scaled up from the dilution: 13,824 distinct products this round can make, times the 300x the project asked for, rounded up.
At that count the chance a named product is missing is 5.09e-131.
round 3 no-donor control should be near empty beside it; its colonies come off the count.

troubleshooting.problem: Fewer net colonies than the count above
troubleshooting.solution: The round has lost library members and no later round can put them back. Electroporate more of the ligation, or run the round again.

troubleshooting.problem: The no-donor control is not empty
troubleshooting.solution: The destination was not opened to completion, or the blunt chopper missed. What grows is the round before's library, one position short, and it reaches the linkage read as truncated members.

steps.title: Round 3: prep the library
instructions: Harvest the whole culture rather than a single colony.
Prep the plasmid and measure the concentration.
notes: Harvesting the whole culture is what keeps the library a library; picking colonies here throws away everything not picked.
expected: One pool of plasmid, 2276 bp per molecule. This is the finished library.
BbsI still cuts it and BsaI no longer does.

troubleshooting.solution: The culture was grown too briefly, or the antibiotic was wrong for this backbone. Check the vector's own marker.

steps.title: Read linkage
instructions: Amplify the whole cargo out of the finished library, from the vector before the first AGGA to the vector past the final TTCC, so one read carries a member's parts and its barcode block together.
Sequence the amplicon as a long read.
Decode each read's block against barcodes.tsv, then read the coding bases beside it against the member that block names.
notes: The block reads in the reverse of the order the rounds ran: each round inserted its barcode ahead of the ones already there.
This plan designs no sequencing primers.
0.0% of the single-base deletions a barcode can carry leave a read another barcode of the same part list could leave, which no read can be assigned through.

Takacsi-Nagy's Figures 1D and 1E read about 95% of their reads carrying a valid barcode at every position, and nearly 90% of the library correctly linked. That is what one source reached, not a mark this library is held to.
expected: A table from barcode combination to cargo: each read decodes to one member of each part list, and the coding bases it carries are that member's.
The 41 bp block reads C, DBD and N, each barcode separated from the last by the cloning scar TTCC, at 1631-1672 of the representative construct.

troubleshooting.problem: A read carries fewer barcodes than there are rounds
troubleshooting.solution: A round did not go in. Check that round's prep against its own record before blaming the sequencing.

troubleshooting.problem: A combination decodes to a member the coding bases are not
troubleshooting.solution: That round joined a block to the wrong barcode, so barcodes.tsv no longer names what the library holds. Rebuild that round rather than carrying the table forward; no later round repairs it.

holes.missing: no primer pair, amplicon length or read depth for either library read
holes.filled_by: whichever way #343 is decided: the plan designs both pairs against the finished record, or the step says what each must span and leaves the pair to the reader

steps.title: Read representation
instructions: Amplify across the 41 bp barcode block alone, forward from the 34 bp internal stuffer every member keeps and back from the vector past the final TTCC.
Sequence the amplicon, decode each read against barcodes.tsv, and count the reads each barcode combination gets.
notes: Read representation again after every later bottleneck — the final assembly, and anything downstream that resamples the library. Linkage is read once; this one is read at each.
The short amplicon is what makes repeating it cheap: linkage spans the whole cargo, this spans the block.

Where you amplify the block to read it, carry any sample index on a primer rather than ligating it on, and keep the barcodes away from where a primer anneals: both cost more read counts than what a barcode spells does.
expected: A count for each of up to 13,824 distinct combinations: how many of them are seen at all, and how evenly they are read.
A combination with no reads is a member the library has lost.

troubleshooting.solution: It was lost at a round or at a bottleneck since, and no later step puts it back. Read the rounds' own titre plates before re-reading this one.
Members differ in length and a bottleneck can favour the short ones. This read measures the skew; nothing here says how much of it is tolerable.

holes.missing: no pass mark for either library read: what share of the library must be seen, how even the counts must be, or what linkage fidelity passes
holes.where: the linkage and representation reads, what carries the library forward
holes.filled_by: the screen downstream, which is what sets the representation the library has to reach

steps.title: Pick the working vector
instructions: Take one tube of the working vector stock for the application this library is built for.
Confirm its own cargo enzyme opens it on AGGA and TTCC, giving up the ccdB cassette the library displaces.
notes: The cargo enzyme is chosen against every molecule in this pot, so it has to be settled before the blocks are designed: a project names it under reserved_extra and no block then spells it.
expected: One opened backbone and the ccdB cassette beside it, and nothing else cut.

holes.missing: no working vector is named, so nothing names the cargo enzyme, its cycling or the final vector's length
holes.where: final assembly, the vector the library moves into
holes.filled_by: the project naming a working vector, which is a stock the lab holds and an application chooses

steps.title: Release the cargo from the library backbone
instructions: Digest the finished library with BsaI and the blunt enzyme that shreds the backbone it leaves.
Heat-kill both. Nothing is purified: the working vector goes into this tube.
notes: The sites that free the cargo belong to the vector the rounds ran in, not to the cargo, so a backbone without them cannot release it.
expected: The whole cargo free, on AGGA and TTCC.

holes.missing: the backbone this library was built in presents no cut that frees its cargo, so no release digest can be written
holes.filled_by: a destination vector carrying the releasing sites outboard of the cargo, as the method's own DMX vector does

holes.missing: every mass in the final assembly is unsourced, the SPRI ratio with them
holes.filled_by: a pilot, or carrying the round's own numbers across and saying so

steps.title: Assemble the cargo into the working vector
instructions: Add the working vector, its cargo enzyme and the ligase to the release tube, and run the enzyme's own Golden Gate cycling.
notes: This is the one reaction where the working vector meets material the rounds made; the rounds all finish first.
expected: One circular final vector a member, the ccdB cassette displaced by the cargo.

holes.missing: no working vector is named, so nothing names the cargo enzyme, its cycling or the final vector's length
holes.where: final assembly, the vector the library moves into
holes.filled_by: the project naming a working vector, which is a stock the lab holds and an application chooses

holes.missing: every mass in the final assembly is unsourced, the SPRI ratio with them
holes.filled_by: a pilot, or carrying the round's own numbers across and saying so

steps.title: Clean the assembly up and electroporate into Endura ElectroCompetent Cells
instructions: Add SPRI paramagnetic beads and elute in water. The ratio is not a sourced one; see the hole.
Pulse at 1800 V, 600 Ω and 10 µF in a 1 mm cuvette.
Recover and grow at 30 °C, as every round did.
cautions: Keep the cells and the cuvette on ice; a warm cuvette arcs.
notes: This is a bottleneck like a round's, and the library can only lose members here. Electroporate all of the assembly rather than a measured part of it.
The settings are the cells' own and are keyed by their catalogue number, not set by this method.
expected: At least 4,147,200 net colonies: 13,824 distinct members times the 300x the project asked for, rounded up.
At that count the chance a named member is missing is 5.09e-131.
Near-empty plates from a no-cargo control beside it; what grows there is working vector that kept its ccdB cassette.

troubleshooting.problem: Fewer net colonies than the count above
troubleshooting.solution: The library has lost members in the transfer. Nothing downstream puts them back; repeat the assembly from more of the released cargo.

holes.missing: every mass in the final assembly is unsourced, the SPRI ratio with them
holes.filled_by: a pilot, or carrying the round's own numbers across and saying so

steps.title: Read representation in the final vector
instructions: Amplify across the barcode block again, exactly as the read before the move did.
Sequence, decode each read against barcodes.tsv, and compare the counts with the read taken in the library backbone.
notes: Linkage is read once, in the library backbone; a barcode still names the same part after the move, because the move carries the whole cargo in one piece.
This read is what the final assembly is judged on, and nothing says what share of the library has to survive it.
expected: The same combinations, at a similar evenness. A combination seen before the move and not after it was lost in the transfer into the working vector.

troubleshooting.problem: Markedly fewer combinations than before the move
troubleshooting.solution: The transfer was the bottleneck, not the rounds. Compare the colony count with the step above before rebuilding anything.
